body.statement: For every finite acquired collection \(E_0\) on which the full correctly typed unconditional CTFIDU\({}^{+}(G,Q,\mathcal R(E_0))\) procedure accepts, there exists a uniform certificate \(E\) using only protocols and slices represented in \(E_0\), with \(\operatorname{Cost}(E)\le\operatorname{Cost}(E_0)\), at most one source-slice record per target factor \(C_j\), at most \(k\) nonempty records, and at most \(k\) distinct protocols. For each factor, its selected protocol, slice, labelled source, and ancestor-district transcript schema succeed simultaneously for every assignment and induced equality type in \(\Omega_j\). Conversely, every uniform certificate accepted by \(\operatorname{Acc}\) induces a complete accepting CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) run on \(\mathcal R(E)\).
body.justification: This quantifier-exchange theorem is the load-bearing bridge from complete fixed-source identification to a compact acquisition certificate and is directly stress-tested by the finite equality-type search.
body.gap: Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026), Algorithm 2 and Appendix E, establish completeness for concrete labelled queries and fixed regimes; they do not prove that one selected source and restriction schema remain valid across every free assignment and equality type of a target factor.
body.consumer: The theorem limits paid acquisitions and auditable source transcripts by the number of target districts rather than the number of value assignments.

obligation.what_is_open: The unproved step is the exchange from branchwise witnesses, \(\forall\omega\in\Omega_j\,\exists(S,\ell,T,\tau)\), to one fixed protocol, slice, source, and transcript satisfying \(\exists(S,\ell,T,\tau)\,\forall\omega\in\Omega_j\).
obligation.obstruction: Neither the published factor loop nor any frozen assumption supplies that exchange. The object \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{norm}}\) is only a proof-handle definition whose construction itself says to prove persistence, so using it would smuggle the theorem into a premise. Equality-type changes alter \(D_T\), and hence can alter both the ancestor set and the obstruction family.
obligation.attempted: I propagated an arbitrary connected obstruction through every ancestor and district restriction, which proves the fixed-label result. Uniform induction then fails at its first step: on two vertices \(u\leftrightarrow v\) and \(u\to v\), with target \(\{v\}\), the matching branch contains \(u\to v\) in \(D_T\) and has obstruction \(\{u,v\}\), while a nonmatching branch deletes that arc and succeeds. No frozen premise proves that a source selected by the complete run avoids such complementary branch behavior.
obligation.partial_result:
For a fixed assignment branch, the obstruction proposition gives a complete local success test and the transcript lemma gives an \(O(|T|^2)\)-bit witness.  Moreover, if one assumes the missing uniform choices
\[
 \forall j\in[k]\;\exists(S_j,\ell_j,T_j,\tau_j)\;
 \forall\omega\in\Omega_j\quad
 (S_j,\ell_j,T_j,\tau_j)\text{ succeeds at }\omega,
\]
then retaining one such record per \(j\) immediately gives at most \(k\) nonempty records and at most \(k\) protocols; all retained protocols came from \(E_0\), and nonnegativity of \(c\) gives \(\operatorname{Cost}(E)\le\operatorname{Cost}(E_0)\).  Conversely, the clauses defining \(\operatorname{Acc}\) directly make the recorded sources successful inputs to the complete factor loop.  Thus only the displayed movement of the source and transcript outside the \(\Omega_j\)-quantifier remains unproved.
